claims.text: A hybrid high-throughput CALPHAD and machine-learning framework can accurately predict melting temperatures for refractory high-entropy alloys.
The hybrid framework can accurately predict entropy of fusion for refractory high-entropy alloys.
Holder means of elemental properties are suitable machine-learning descriptors for melting properties.
The target refractory HEAs are disordered BCC or FCC solid solutions at equiatomic or near-equiatomic compositions.
High-throughput CALPHAD can screen thousands of multicomponent compositions for phase fractions and melting temperatures.
Machine-learning regression using elemental and structural descriptors can refine predictions of melting temperature, entropy of fusion, and heat capacity where experimental data are sparse.
The method should be restricted to elements and composition ranges covered reliably by the thermodynamic database.
Positive Fe-Cr and Co-Cr mixing enthalpies can promote miscibility gaps and phase separation in Cr-containing HEAs.
The disordered BCC or FCC lattice is stabilized by solid-solution strengthening.
The distribution of high-melting W and Ta relative to lower-melting V and Cr influences segregation and local melting behavior.
CALPHAD efficiently calculates phase equilibria from thermodynamic databases over large compositional spaces.
Holder-mean descriptors capture statistical physics associated with atomic packing and FCC-HCP transitions.
Melting behavior is governed primarily by collective elemental properties rather than specific binary interactions when phase separation is absent.
First-principles calculations are computationally prohibitive for screening vast multicomponent composition spaces.
The hybrid method will predict refractory-HEA melting temperatures within ±5% of experimental values.
High-throughput CALPHAD can identify HEA candidates with melting temperatures above 1250 °C and specified phase fractions.
The hybrid method will be faster than standard non-automated CALPHAD for screening large composition spaces.
The hybrid method will be more accurate than DFT for melting properties of disordered alloys.
For Al-Cr-Fe-Mn-Ti alloys, Al below 25 at.% is a database-valid boundary for the method.
Training on ordered compounds can reduce machine-learning reliability when predicting properties of disordered HEAs affected by lattice distortion.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that the method is valid only within reliable database limits, but the proposed decisive falsification test deliberately selects a composition outside those limits. Failure there would test an excluded domain rather than falsify the stated in-domain hypothesis.
